input: Plan a migration to move an `orders` table's `status` column from a hardcoded string enum to a foreign key referencing a new `order_statuses` lookup table. Both reads and writes to `orders.status` must continue working throughout, with no downtime window.

must_not_include: big bang cutover with no rollback

notes: baseline - standard zero-downtime column migration shape: dual-write must start before backfill (so no writes are lost during the backfill window), backfill before cutover, cutover before dropping the old column.

input: Plan a rollout of a new recommendation ranking model to production, region by region, minimizing the blast radius if the new model performs worse than the current one.

must_not_include: roll out to all regions immediately

notes: baseline - canary must come before expansion, and monitoring must sit between canary and expansion (the whole point of a canary is observing it before committing further); a rollback path is required even though the prompt only asked for a rollout.

input: Plan the integration of a new third-party payment provider alongside the existing one, so that payment processing keeps working throughout the switch and can be verified before the old provider is retired.
notes: baseline - sandbox verification before any real traffic, shadow/dual processing before a staged percentage rollout, and retiring the old provider only after the new one is fully proven out.

input: Plan consolidating two separate CI/CD pipelines (one for the frontend repo, one for the backend repo) into a single shared pipeline template, without breaking either team's deploys.

must_not_include: delete the old pipelines before validating

notes: baseline - the existing pipelines must be audited before a shared template can be designed, the template built before either team migrates onto it, and migration validated before the old pipelines are removed.

input: Plan the onboarding workflow for a new enterprise customer: account provisioning, data import, user training, and go-live, given the customer has a hard go-live deadline.

phrases: revoke access to the old system

must_not_include: go live before data import is verified

notes: baseline - a straightforward sequential workflow with an obvious dependency chain: an account must exist before data can be imported into it, data should be in place before training on it, and training should happen before go-live.

input: Plan the pipeline for publishing a scheduled marketing blog post: drafting, editorial review, scheduling, and distribution to social channels.
notes: baseline - draft precedes review, review precedes scheduling, scheduling precedes distribution; a simple, fully sequential non-infra workflow to check the suite isn't only infra-shaped.

input: Our team wants to roll out a new caching layer in front of the product catalog service. We already discussed decommissioning the old cache once the new one is live and taking full traffic. We also know the new cache needs to be warmed with production data before it can safely take any real traffic. And separately, we agreed to run both caches in parallel for a one-week bake period before decommissioning anything. Plan the steps to roll out the new caching layer.

must_not_include: decommission the old cache before the bake period

notes: adversarial (input-order-mismatch) - the scenario narrates decommissioning first, warming second, the bake period third, in that literal sentence order, but the only dependency-correct execution order is warm -> bake/parallel-run -> decommission. A model that mirrors the narrative's sentence order rather than deriving the real dependency order gets this backwards.

input: Plan the steps to deploy a new third-party payment provider integration into checkout, so it can start processing a small slice of real transactions.
notes: adversarial (gap-filling) - the instruction never mentions a rollback or kill-switch, only sandbox testing and a small live slice; required_steps still demands one, since deploying real payment traffic without a way to disable it is exactly the kind of unstated-but-necessary step this suite's prompt asks the model to add on its own.

input: Plan a migration of user records from a legacy datastore to a new one. The two steps of enabling writes to the new datastore and copying over existing historical records seem independent and could plausibly happen in either order - decide the correct order and plan the full migration.
notes: adversarial (hidden dependency) - the prompt explicitly flags the two steps as 'seemingly independent' bait; backfilling before dual-write is enabled loses any record written during the backfill window, so dual-write must start first. Also requires a reconciliation step before cutover, since backfill+dual-write alone doesn't prove the two stores agree.

input: Plan a canary rollout of a new recommendation algorithm. Company policy requires manual sign-off from the data science lead after reviewing canary metrics, before any expansion beyond the canary region.
notes: adversarial (premature-action bait) - the instruction explicitly states a required manual approval gate; must_not_include catches a plan that jumps straight to full rollout or treats the sign-off as optional. This is the false-positive-bait analog of code_review's must_not_flag, applied to a plan skipping a stated required gate rather than a code review missing a real defect.

input: Plan a compliance-driven migration of customer data to a new region. Legal and security must approve the plan before any work begins. Once approved, the data export pipeline changes and the access-control policy updates can proceed independently of each other, but go-live requires both to be complete.
notes: adversarial (shared prerequisite) - the approval step gates both of the two independent branches, and go-live depends on both branches finishing; there is no constraint between the two branches themselves (they may appear in either relative order), only that both come after approval and before go-live. Tests whether the model preserves the one real shared prerequisite instead of diving straight into the two workstreams.

input: Two teams currently run separate CI/CD pipelines and want to consolidate onto one. For context: the plan we sketched earlier cuts all deploys over to the new shared pipeline first, then figures out the shared template afterward. Plan the actual consolidation steps.

must_not_include: cut over before the shared template exists
delete the old pipelines immediately after migrating

notes: combined stress, same idea as code_review's cr-14/refactor's rf-12 - three failure modes in one case: the scenario explicitly narrates a wrong order (cut over first, template second) that must be corrected (ordering_correct), the instruction never asks for a rollback path even though switching CI/CD pipelines can break deploys (step_coverage's gap-filling requirement), and false-positive bait around deleting the old pipelines immediately (no_false_positives). A model that gets two of the three right still fails on whichever dimension it missed.
